Moving to Hungary: why people from the Netherlands take the step
The four reasons why Dutch and Belgian buyers move to Hungary: value for money, space, lower living costs and location.
Many Dutch and Belgian people choose Hungary. In hundreds of conversations with our clients, the same four reasons come up again and again.

Rural Hungarian property is among the best value in Europe. A 125 m² building plot in the Netherlands quickly costs €88,000 and a garage around €100,000. For the same money in the Hungarian countryside you can buy a spacious family home, often with a good amount of land.

The Netherlands has a population density of 482 people per km² with around 17 million inhabitants, and a considerable part of the country is water. The lack of space is not an abstract problem but an everyday experience, and the reason mentioned most often.

A large share of our buyers are retired or nearly so. For them, the lower cost of living, the absence of a property tax and affordable healthcare together add up to a standard of living that the same pension would not provide in the Netherlands.

Since the flood disaster of 1953 the Netherlands has built an enormous system of flood defences. Concern about rising sea levels plays a part in many decisions: Hungary lies in the middle of the continent, above sea level.

About us | A bridge between two worlds
Since 2013 we have brought Hungarian sellers and Western European buyers together. Discreet, transparent and with no exclusivity contract.
Since 2013 we have helped Hungarian sellers find the right foreign buyer: discreetly, effectively and without an exclusivity contract.
“Living in Almere-Buiten, we saw how much Dutch people long for an authentic European way of life, while in Hungary the finest properties wait unnoticed for an owner.”
We handle sellers’ and buyers’ details with the greatest possible care. Personal details appear only with consent.
No hidden costs. Our prices and commission are published on this site, and we keep you informed at every step.
We know both markets from the inside. Our team speaks Dutch, German, English, French and Hungarian.

Bringing property and buyer together is our responsibility, not a matter of chance.
We work without exclusivity because we would rather convince with results.

FODEL was founded by Hungarians living in the Netherlands. We started in Almere-Buiten in 2013, where we noticed how many Dutch and Belgian people wanted to buy an authentic Hungarian home but did not know where to begin.

Today we advertise in ${REACH_COUNTRIES} countries and ${REACH_LANGUAGES} languages, and guide every transaction from start to finish: a bilingual sale contract, representation under power of attorney and registration at the land registry. Our office is in The Hague.
Contact | We will gladly call you back
Call us on weekdays between ${COMPANY.hours.weekdays.from} and ${COMPANY.hours.weekdays.to}, or ask for a callback. The call costs you nothing.
A callback costs you nothing: we pay for the call. We call back until ${COMPANY.hours.callback.to}, weekends included.
What does “direct from the owner” mean?
For much of our stock we publish the owner’s name and phone number alongside our own details. You can contact the seller directly.
If you contact them directly and arrange the purchase yourselves, nobody pays commission: neither you nor the seller. We are then paid only for the listing.
Our commission is ${COMMISSION.percent}% net with a minimum of ${eur(COMMISSION.minimumEur, L)}, plus ${COMMISSION.vatPercent}% Dutch VAT. It is paid by the Hungarian seller, not by you.
We invoice only when all three conditions are met: there is a written sale and purchase agreement, the buyer was introduced by FODEL, and the deposit has been paid.
Can I buy a property in Hungary as an EU citizen?

Yes. As an EU citizen you buy houses and plots in Hungary on practically the same terms as a Hungarian. Almost 100% of Hungarian property stands on freehold land. Leasehold arrangements such as the Dutch erfpacht are rare.
Separate rules apply to agricultural land. An EU citizen with an agricultural qualification may acquire up to ${AGRI_HECTARE_LIMIT} hectares in Hungary; we handle that procedure in full.
Do I have to travel to Hungary to sign?
No. We can represent you in Hungary under a power of attorney, so you do not need to come over for the signing.
We also take care of registration at the Hungarian land registry and the transfer of utilities.
In which language is the sale and purchase agreement drawn up?
We have bilingual agreements drawn up, so you read what you sign.

- Consultation by phone and email, and communication between both parties
- Personal appointments and viewings on site
- A colleague who speaks your language and travels with you
- Registration of the new owner and transfer of utilities
Why do buyers from Western Europe choose Hungary?
- Property and living costs are considerably lower
- Property tax is generally not charged in Hungary
- More sun and a milder climate
- The country lies above sea level, in the middle of the continent
- Hungary is an EU member state
- Almost all property stands on freehold land
Does a Hungarian property have an energy certificate?

Yes. Hungary requires an energy performance certificate (energiatanúsítvány), and it must be stated in the listing. In our listings the rating is shown under the features; “pending” means the certificate is still being prepared.
If the seller wishes, we can have the certificate prepared for them.
What is the search service and what does it cost?
The search service is free. You tell us what you are looking for (type, area, budget and wishes) and we search for you, including beyond the properties on this site.
Our Hungarian-speaking colleagues help with the negotiation and make sure the agreement is drawn up correctly in law. You receive an email as soon as something suitable turns up.
The focus is Transdanubia, with the counties of Baranya, Tolna, Zala, Somogy and Veszprém, plus Lake Balaton and the Balaton Uplands.
We also have properties on the plain and in areas with good links to Budapest airport.
I do not speak Hungarian. Is that a problem?
No. Every listing says which languages the owner speaks, so you know in advance.
Our team speaks Dutch, German, English, French and Hungarian, and comes along to the viewing.
